context: Do short-lived insects gain experience?
utterance: Just to point out that insects with very short lives have far higher temporal resolution than we do, so the world around them goes in slow motion. The tradeoff for this is that it's metabolically expensive, hence the short life, but from the frame of reference of the insect, they lived a long time. We tend to think that our perception of time is the norm, but every species experiences the world at different rates.

context: ELI5 Why or how do medicines have two names? How do they pick the "generic" name?
utterance: The “generic” name is the actual name (or sometimes a shortened version) of the chemical compound that makes up the medication. The brand name is a marketing name invented by the pharmaceutical company that patented it that’s easier to say/remember.

context: ELI5 Why or how do medicines have two names? How do they pick the "generic" name?
utterance: Generic names follow the rules of the [international nonproprietary name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_nonproprietary_name) system created by the WHO. They are created from a system of stems and affixes according to the drug's use and chemical properties, e.g. the suffix "-caine" is used for local anaesthetics and "-vir" is used for antivirals.

context: What rocks are mountains most commonly made of and how can I determine that?
utterance: There's a lot of long answers here. The short answer is Granite (white --> whitish), or basalt (black). Granite is super common, and because of the geochemical stability of silica (common in granite) you end up with a lot of silica sand (white) after a fuckload of time. Basalt gives you black sand, and is less common. I'm a geochemist.

context: What rocks are mountains most commonly made of and how can I determine that?
utterance: Here on Earth, mountains are made of all kinds of different rocks, but the vast majority of sand is quartz sand because A) quartz is extremely common in many different rocks, and B) it is one of the minerals most resistant to weathering, both physical and chemical. Other sands exist (green olivine sand in Hawai'i and shell sand on tropical islands are two examples) but quartz is by far the most common. Source: I have a Geology degree and am a science teacher.

context: When your brain releases hormones like adrenaline, endorphin, dopamine etc that have an almost instant effect, are they just conjured on the spot or created in advance and stored somewhere to just wait for the signal?
utterance: When people take MDMA too much over time their serotonin glands can become depleted, so yes you absolutely can run out. Your body produces these chemicals very slowly, storing them until needed. When the appropriate stimulation happens, your nerves initiate a biochemical process that opens the gland and releases the hormone. Then, there is another biochemical feedback mechanism that closes the gland afterwards.

context: When your brain releases hormones like adrenaline, endorphin, dopamine etc that have an almost instant effect, are they just conjured on the spot or created in advance and stored somewhere to just wait for the signal?
utterance: Yes they are stored in vesicles (little bubbles in the cells), and not all of them originate in the brain. Adrenalin, as the name says, comes from the adrenal gland, which is next to ("ad") the kidney ("ren"). And yes you can run out, which happens with certain hormones when there's a deficiency in the production or for example during prolonged stress (severe injuries etc). They have to be supplemented then.
